title: Emile Berliner built a telephone microphone and a flat disc record that became the recording standard

paragraphs.text: Emile Berliner was born on May 20, 1851.
He was born into a Jewish merchant family.
According to the Library of Congress, his father was a merchant and a Talmudic scholar, and his mother was an amateur musician.
In 1870, when he was not yet 20, he emigrated to the United States to avoid conscription in the Franco-Prussian War.
In Washington he worked as a clerk in a store selling fabrics and textile goods.
In New York he obtained a position as general cleanup man in the laboratory of Constantine Fahlberg, the discoverer of saccharine.
According to the German Patent and Trade Mark Office (DPMA), Emil Berliner was born in Hanover in 1851.
According to the Library of Congress, in 1876, during the American centennial celebrations, Berliner saw a demonstration of Alexander Graham Bell's telephone.
Berliner thought that one of the telephone's weaknesses was its transmitter.
He created a new type of transmitter, a type of microphone, which increased the volume of the transmitted voice.
He wrote the caveat application to the Patent Office himself, without a patent attorney.
According to the National Inventors Hall of Fame, he sold the patent to the fledgling Bell Telephone Company.
According to the German National Library, the sum he received from Bell gave him the financial independence to continue his work as an inventor.
His microphone was so successful that it replaced the earlier microphone in Bell's telephones.
His design is still the basis for most microphones manufactured today.

stations.title: The gramophone and the flat disc

paragraphs.text: In 1881, while working in Boston, Berliner became an American citizen, and in the same year he married Cora Adler.
He later left Bell and continued to work as an independent researcher and inventor.
In 1887 Berliner was granted a patent for the gramophone, a device to record and reproduce sounds.
According to the Hall of Fame, the gramophone used a flat disc rather than the cylinder proposed by Edison.
According to the German National Library, Edison was at the time unable to come up with a functioning completed model, and his records were not intended for mass production.
According to Encyclopedia.com, Berliner introduced the lateral method, in which the needle moves from left to right.
According to the DPMA, lateral recording in a spiral groove made it possible to improve the sound, expand its range and duplicate more easily.
The switch to flat discs improved sound quality, and they could be mass-produced at a much lower cost.
According to the German Patent and Trade Mark Office (DPMA), the American patent for the gramophone was granted on November 8, 1887.

stations.title: The gramophone goes out into the world

paragraphs.text: According to Samuel Brylawski, Berliner saw the gramophone as a home-entertainment device, while others focused on office use for dictation.
On May 16, 1888, he delivered a lecture on the gramophone at the Franklin Institute.
There he said that future generations would be able to condense into twenty minutes a tone picture of an entire lifetime.
In 1889 he traveled to Germany, demonstrated the gramophone and reached an agreement with the toy firm Kammerer and Reinhardt to manufacture it.
In the United States, with investors' money, he founded the United States Gramophone Company.
In 1896 Eldridge Johnson introduced a spring motor in place of the hand crank, and sales improved dramatically.
In December 1898 Berliner and his brother Joseph founded Deutsche Grammophon in Hanover.
His trademark was a painting of a dog listening to His Master's Voice, and it was later adopted by RCA.
Encyclopedia.com: in 1893, with investments from friends and acquaintances
Berliner did not invent recorded sound technology, but his innovations led to its mass distribution.
The published records are one of the first successful attempts to mass-market popular sound recordings.
His flat discs eventually replaced Edison's fragile and unwieldy cylinders.
Berliner's flat disc became the standard for mass-produced commercial recordings, and the precursor of the digital compact disc.
According to the DPMA, for almost 100 years the vinyl record remained the standard sound reproduction technology.

stations.title: Health, science and the Land of Israel

paragraphs.text: In 1900 his youngest daughter, Alice, fell seriously ill, and as a result Berliner campaigned against the high mortality rate of babies and children.
In 1909 he donated funds for an infirmary building at a tuberculosis sanitarium in Washington Grove, dedicated to the memory of his father.
In 1919 he and his associates published a book of drawings and rhymes about children who neglect cleanliness.
In 1924 he established the Bureau of Health Education, to promote hygiene and health education for mothers and children.
He also established a fellowship named after his mother.
Zionism was another cause in which Berliner was deeply involved.
According to The Jewish Press, he was president of the Washington Zionist district and a large contributor to institutions in the Land of Israel, among them the Hebrew University.
In 1926 he received a patent for acoustic tiles.
He was also a composer, acoustician, aviation pioneer and public-health advocate.
In 1929 Berliner received a medal from the Franklin Institute.
According to The Jewish Press, President Hoover praised him.
He was inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame as the inventor of the microphone that was part of the first Bell telephones, and for his gramophone, the first record player to use discs.
Emile Berliner died on August 3, 1929, in his 79th year.
According to The Jewish Press, he later became an agnostic, but remained a proud Jew.
According to the DPMA, Klara, the daughter of his brother Joseph, was murdered as a Jew in the Theresienstadt concentration camp in 1943.
According to The Jewish Press, it is incredible that this great man has been all but forgotten.
According to the DPMA, Berliner's patent claims were neither detailed nor comprehensive, so many imitators circumvented the protection relatively easily.
In June 1900 an injunction shut down the Berliner Gramophone Company of Philadelphia and left Berliner with no way to operate.
Berliner passed the patent rights to Johnson, who formed the Victor company, and retained a financial interest in it.
Berliner set up a company in Montreal.
According to Encyclopedia.com, the Montreal company manufactured 2,000 records in its first year, and sold over two million records in 1901.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה.קום, אביו של ברלינר היה איש מכירות ואמו טיפלה בו ובעשרה אחיו.
claims.quote: His father, Samuel, was a salesman, while his mother, Sarah, cared for young Emile and his ten siblings.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה.קום, ברלינר מכר את הזכויות לחברת בל בבוסטון תמורת 75,000 דולר, ויש מקורות שמדווחים על 50,000.
claims.quote: Berliner sold the rights to his invention to the Bell Telephone Company of Boston three months later for $75,000 (some sources report $50,000).

claims.text: לפי המשרד הגרמני לפטנטים וסימני מסחר (DPMA), אמיל ברלינר נולד בהנובר ב-1851.
claims.quote: Emil Berliner was born in Hanover in 1851

claims.text: לפי המשרד הגרמני לפטנטים וסימני מסחר (DPMA), הפטנט האמריקאי על הגרמופון ניתן ב-8 בנובמבר 1887.
claims.quote: The invention became better known under the title of its American patent, also granted effective November 8, 1887

claims.text: הוא נולד ב-1851 למשפחת סוחרים יהודית.
claims.quote: V Samuel (1813–72), Kaufmann und Schriftgelehrter, S des Moses (1786–1854)

claims.text: הוא נולד ב-1851 למשפחת סוחרים יהודית.
claims.quote: Elektroingenieur, * 20.5.1851 Hannover, † 3.8.1929 Washington.

claims.quote: Being of Jewish heritage, he gave financial support for the rebuilding of Palestine and was instrumental in the founding of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

claims.text: הוא נולד למשפחת סוחרים יהודית.

claims.text: אחר כך עזב את בל והמשיך לעבוד כחוקר וממציא עצמאי.
claims.quote: He left the company in 1884 to return to Washington to pursue his dream of becoming a private inventor.

claims.text: בארצות הברית הקים, בכסף של משקיעים, את חברת הגרמופון של ארצות הברית.
claims.quote: Returning to America, Berliner entered into an agreement with several New York backers

claims.text: בארצות הברית הקים, בכסף של משקיעים, את חברת הגרמופון של ארצות הברית.
claims.quote: the more lucrative United States Gramophone Company in Washington, D.C.

claims.text: בדצמבר 1898 ייסד ברלינר עם אחיו יוסף את דויטשה גרמופון בהנובר.
claims.quote: Deutsche Grammophon was founded in Hanover on December 6, 1898.

claims.text: בדצמבר 1898 ייסד ברלינר עם אחיו יוסף את דויטשה גרמופון בהנובר.
claims.quote: Its directors are Emil Berliner, the inventor of the record and the gramophone, and his brother Joseph.

claims.text: לפי DPMA, קלרה, בתו של אחיו יוסף, נרצחה כיהודייה במחנה הריכוז תרזיינשטט ב-1943.
claims.quote: Joseph Berliner's daughter and heiress Klara was murdered as a Jew in the Theresienstadt concentration camp in 1943.

claims.text: עבד בחברת בל עד 1883 וחזר לוושינגטון כחוקר עצמאי
claims.quote: After returning to the U.S., Berliner left the telephone business in 1883 and set to work in his Washington laboratory.

claims.text: ב-1908, מלגת המחקר שרה ברלינר
claims.quote: In honor of his mother, he established the Sarah Berliner Research Fellowship for physics, biology, and chemistry in 1908.
